subject.title: Telegram voice message delayed ~15 minutes before agent dispatch, then run aborts

question: What narrow Telegram reliability contract should OpenClaw implement for delayed voice-message dispatch followed by an aborted/no-reply turn?
rationale: The source gaps are real, but choosing the latency threshold, restart versus alert behavior, retry/fallback semantics, and visible failure text requires maintainer intent before a safe repair lane can run.

options.title: Define watchdog plus fallback contract
options.body: Choose a source-age threshold, diagnostic/restart behavior, and visible aborted-turn fallback, then implement it with focused tests and live Telegram proof.

options.title: Wait for live repro first
options.body: Keep the issue open without code changes until a real Telegram replay identifies the exact boundary that produced the 14-minute delay and abort.

options.title: Split into existing trackers
options.body: Move only the polling-sleep part to the open polling PR and only the recovery-reply part to the voice recovery issue, leaving this issue for any remaining exact repro evidence.

recommendation.title: Define watchdog plus fallback contract
recommendation.body: Choose a source-age threshold, diagnostic/restart behavior, and visible aborted-turn fallback, then implement it with focused tests and live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the best available owner for the product contract choice because the decision spans Telegram liveness, voice/audio behavior, and user-visible fallback policy.
